## Overview

The May 10, 2026 guide describes two Dashboard views. It presents Radar Analytics center as the default in Radar Overview and shows how the New overview toggle returns to the legacy view. The November 7, 2026 capture keeps the Dashboard fraud-analysis purpose and links the same two routes. The reporting details below come from May. Fraud Insights, Sigma and Data Pipeline are separate analysis routes. See May lines 8–27 and 159–165.

## May Radar Analytics center

The newer view defaults to the prior 30 days of transaction history after a 24-hour delay. Users can choose their date range, count or payment volume, fraud-arrival date or payment date, retry deduplication per PaymentIntent, and optional SetupIntent inclusion. See May lines 30–48.

- **Fraud.** The panel distinguishes fraud disputes from early fraud warnings that have yet to escalate to disputes. It shows observed rates and an optional modeled worst-case line based on historical arrival patterns. The estimate toggle may be absent at low fraud volume or when using fraud-arrival date. Late disputes can change observed rates.
- **Disputes.** Distinguishes fraud from other dispute categories. The May formula is disputed payments of any type divided by successful payments in the same period. Nonfraud reasons do not enter the fraud rate.
- **Blocks.** Breaks out high-risk and custom-rule blocks. The May newer-view prose divides all blocked payments by successful payments. The legacy view uses attempted payments as its denominator.

The panels show comparable-business and regional benchmarks. See May lines 50–102.

**Rule matches** reports actions actually taken on screened transactions. Transactions shows each action's rate, count and volume. Blocked shows top matched block rules, and 3DS shows authentication outcomes. Allow distinguishes legitimate, fraud-disputed or early-fraud-warning, and refunded transactions. Review shows currently in review, approved, rejected, failed and disputed. A filed dispute replaces an earlier in-review or approved classification in this panel. See May lines 104–157.

## May Legacy Radar overview

- **Overview Chart.** Shows attempted payments through 3DS challenge outcomes, Radar screening and disputes.
- **Benchmarks.** Shows regional and, when available, similar-business block, fraudulent-dispute and estimated false-positive rates. Similar-business benchmarks display for cohorts with many dozens of businesses, and inclusion requires a significant number of payments. Each business contributes equal weight for a given benchmark. Contact Stripe to opt out of contributing data. Opted-out businesses can continue to view benchmarks.
- **Fraud prevention.** Attempted payments count supported screened requests including retries. Legacy block rate divides blocked payments by attempted payments. Legacy counts exclude screened SetupIntents, which the newer chart can optionally display. High-risk and custom-rule blocks have separate counts, rates and volumes. The estimated false-positive rate models Radar blocking a nonfraudulent payment.
- **Fraudulent disputes and all disputes.** The fraudulent-dispute chart uses payment creation date and, for the trailing 120 days, distinguishes the observed partial rate from the modeled possible maximum. The disputes-received chart uses dispute creation date for successful payments in the selected period. It counts inquiries when they escalate, shows open disputes, disputed volume excluding fees and win rate, and provides a download for the full dispute-reason breakdown.
- **Manual reviews.** The separate Radar for Fraud Teams panel shows the queue and currently in review, approved, refunded and disputed outcomes, plus the disputed share of approved reviews. A customer's dispute of a payment currently in review automatically closes that review.

The May legacy attempted-payment section says card-present Terminal and recurring Stripe Billing payments are not screened. The separate May Risk evaluations guide says the Radar model scores only the initial payment of a recurring Billing subscription and evaluates rules for all payments. This leaves the relationship between the legacy reporting wording and the general scoring and rule behavior unresolved. See May analytics lines 163–275 and [[source-stripe-radar-risk-evaluation]].

## Availability, export and monitoring

The May legacy section describes daily computation starting at midnight UTC, data available within 24 hours, a six-month default and daily foreign exchange rates for monetary aggregation in the account's default currency. Each chart offers a CSV download. Users with Sigma access can open the generating SQL through View in Sigma. See May lines 277–293.

May describes Radar analytics comparing fraud and dispute rates with card-network monitoring thresholds and showing current status and program details, including possible penalties. A current program status, an observed rate and a modeled estimate convey different information. See May lines 295–299 and [[stripe-dispute-monitoring-programs]].

radar-analytics.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/radar/analytics establishes Dashboard fraud analytics navigation to Radar Analytics center and Legacy Radar overview (new raw lines 5-14). It does not freshly describe metric behavior. The May 10 guide describes the newer view as default, with 30 days of history after a 24-hour delay, selection of count or volume, fraud-arrival or payment date, retry deduplication and optional SetupIntents. Fraud, all disputes and blocks are distinct charts. The newer Blocks ratio uses successful payments, while legacy block rate uses attempted payments. Modeled worst-case fraud is conditional and distinct from observed rates (old raw lines 17-48 and 62-102, old raw lines 200-232). The newer Rule matches review outcomes are separate from the legacy Manual reviews panel, which is for Radar for Fraud Teams users and automatically closes a current review if the customer disputes the payment (old raw lines 264-275). Legacy also covers the 3DS/screening/dispute flow, privacy-gated benchmark cohorts, six-month default, exports and daily updates (old raw lines 104-199 and 235-299). source-stripe-radar-analytics.md dates the core views and records the Sigma access prerequisite, benchmark limits and action and metric distinctions. These are reporting states rather than payment or monitoring program outcomes for a particular account.
radar-analytics.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/analytics, the November 7, 2026 difference is presentation and navigation: the full May 10 guide had embedded Radar Analytics center and legacy views, and November links the same query routes (new raw lines 9-14, old raw lines 17-23 and 159-165). Neither a product behavior change nor removal of May functionality is evidenced. Preserve the dated 30-day and six-month defaults, 24-hour lag, version-scoped SetupIntent and screened-payment treatment, denominator differences, conditional estimate visibility, similar-business cohort qualifications and continued viewing after opting out, and Sigma permission separate from CSV (old raw lines 30-48 and 62-95, old raw lines 189-232 and 277-299). Preserve the May 10 recurring Billing wording conflict: legacy attempted-payments prose says recurring Stripe Billing payments are not screened (old raw lines 205-207), while the separate Risk evaluations guide says model scoring covers the initial subscription payment and rules evaluate all payments (raw/stripe-radar-risk-evaluation-2026.md lines 38–42). These are source-specific reporting and general scoring/rule statements, and the November selector does not resolve their relationship. The revised source-stripe-radar-analytics.md records these baseline qualifications as dated May evidence. Keep both dated raw routes and the existing reciprocal Stripe Radar concept and source links, through the root/provider indexes, and retain the separate dispute measurement and card monitoring routes.

concept_suggestions.anchor:
Dashboard → Radar Overview. Two views: new Analytics Center (default) and Legacy overview (toggle).

**New view**: Fraud/Disputes/Blocks rate charts with peer benchmark comparison; rule match breakdown (Blocked/3DS/Allow/Review details); monitoring program status tracking. Configurable: volume vs count, fraud arrival date, de-duplicate retries, include SetupIntents. 24-hour delay; defaults to prior 30 days.

**Legacy view**: Overview Chart (3DS→Screened→Disputed flow), benchmarks (block rate, fraud dispute rate, false positive estimate), fraudulent disputes chart with projected maximum (dashed line). Each chart has CSV download + View in Sigma. See [[source-stripe-radar-analytics]].
concept_suggestions.proposed_markdown:
**May 10, 2026 Radar Overview.** Radar Analytics center was the default, with a toggle to the Legacy overview. The newer view defaults to 30 days after a 24-hour delay. It offers count or volume, fraud arrival or payment date, retry deduplication and optional SetupIntent inclusion. Fraud, all disputes, blocks and rule actions have separate panels.

**Legacy overview.** The six-month default includes the 3DS, Radar screening and dispute sequence, privacy-gated benchmark comparisons, modeled dispute projections and manual reviews for Radar for Fraud Teams. Legacy block rate uses attempted payments, while the newer view's May formula uses successful payments. Charts offer CSV download. View in Sigma requires Sigma access. The November capture links both views. See [[source-stripe-radar-analytics]].
warnings: May raw lines 17–48, 62–102, 159–232 and 264–299 establish dated reporting, access and view boundaries.
